# Tally visibility audit

Read-only inventory: 2026-10-30T10:39:55.883Z. Database: mehta_electronics_local. No raw data values or credentials are included.

## Diagnosis before UI changes

- Direct XML is reachable and returned one open company on 30 October 2026. This proves connectivity, not a completed import.
- Connector imports populate tally_ledgers and tally_stock_items, while legacy tally_customers and tally_items are empty. The native ControlDesk Tally link falls back to the legacy app root.
- Master API searches only name/parent and projects a small subset of stored columns. Stored raw_record JSONB already preserves all parsed fields for groups, ledgers and stock items.
- Item closing_rate_text is exposed without financial authorization in both master and stored APIs.
- Latest connector job stalled; two prior jobs stored. Zero quarantined rows. No structured vouchers delivered. Report XML is retained without normalized report rows.
- No durable source discriminator distinguishes Tally Engine from Bizgenix. Their individual last-sync status cannot be inferred from connector profile names. Show Unknown, not a fabricated source or successful sync.
- Next scheduled connector sync and connector retry attempts are not recorded. Unknown is different from zero. Direct XML job states, where present, appear below.
- Existing browser verification scripts write real-schema sessions/audits; they must be moved to random test schemas before execution.

## Delivery gaps and implementation plan

Company metadata beyond name/GUID is not imported. Stock groups, categories, units, godowns, price levels and cost centres need connector export collections; none has a dedicated imported table. Ledger registration/state/credit/bank fields and item HSN/GST/alternate-unit/price-list/godown fields can only be shown when present in raw data. Preserve and index unknown fields automatically.

Vouchers: Awaiting voucher data. Request structured VOUCHER records with date, GUID/master ID, voucher type/number, ledger entries, inventory entries, amounts and taxes. Do not substitute report totals for vouchers.

Use an additive append-only field index and replay immutable stored payloads into that index, never overwrite imported rows. Capture subsequent master imports into the same index. Separate financial and nonfinancial projections before search, sorting, counts, details or export. Nonfinancial unknown tags fail closed. Native browsers must use stored Tally IDs and show source, timestamps and incomplete coverage. Reconciliation by exact name in the existing service is not identity-safe and requires replacement with durable ID links.

<!-- tally-visibility-verified -->

## Implemented and verified coverage

The baseline MISSING marks above describe the original defect. All delivered fields below now have an indexed field, a selectable browser column, search, detail/history access and server export for Owner/Accounts. Nonfinancial access is fail-closed; unknown or financial XML paths remain restricted. No raw payload or original master row was rewritten by migration/backfill.

The native `/tally` route replaces the legacy-root fallback. Browse latest records or **Every imported sync snapshot**; the latter also searches/exports historical field values. Detail drawers select the exact snapshot, show all fields and changes, and link original XML. Saved views retain filters, sort, snapshot mode and selected columns. Density follows account preferences.

Controller/service/repository layers are `tally-visibility-routes.js`, `tally-visibility-service.js`, and `tally-visibility-repository.js`, behind the contracts in `tally-visibility-contracts.d.ts`. The shared `public/tally-entity-descriptors.js` drives API fields, columns, detail rows and formatting. Migrations 0023–0028 add derived history, permission projections, search indexes, display helpers, explicit CRM ID links, company identity aliases and source observations. Receiver imports preserve existing raw master/quarantine rows; newer state is appended to the index. Replay is idempotent and writes only that index.

CSV and Excel Spreadsheet XML (`.xml`, literal string cells) exports include every filtered page, preserve decimal text, neutralize spreadsheet formulas, check every requested column against the server projection, and write an audit event. Reconciliation creates explicit company/entity/Tally-ID links; names never create a link. Existing name-only legacy mappings are deliberately not treated as verified ID links.

Read-only verification: 2026-10-30T12:36:42.788Z. 24 payload SHA-256 hashes verified; 5419262 parsed raw leaves verified. Stock coverage: 0 valued / 10988 unvalued / 10988 total (partial).

### Data still awaiting delivery/deployment

An actual read-only full-field XML export has now recovered Company, Group, Ledger, StockItem, StockGroup, StockCategory, Unit and Godown collections. The incomplete run honestly remains failed because PriceLevel timed out before CostCentre was attempted; any separately scoped CostCentre result is recorded in its own import report. Original source rows were preserved, with recovered fields appended to history. See `tally-master-coverage-import.json`. The checked-in Windows connector requests full master methods and optional collections, and its Core project builds, but the installed Windows service has not been replaced. Deploy that build for ongoing full-field imports.

Historical Engine/Bizgenix source IDs, retry attempts and next-sync schedule were not stored and remain Unknown. New source-labelled uploads retain their provenance and reported retry metadata. Vouchers remain **Awaiting voucher data**: implement a read-only voucher export carrying stable IDs, dates, ledger/inventory/tax entries and invoice references; add paginated connector transport, replay and reconciliation. Invoices need those voucher entries and references; no invoice data is fabricated. Quarantine replay preserves original rows and reasons.

The existing real-schema browser verifiers were not run because they create sessions/audits in real data. The existing static verifier failed on its stale badge-route mock. The new verifier uses real HTTP/API/UI with a random test schema and drops that schema afterwards.
